newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers stable, Med rates consolidate.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers stable, Med rates consolidate.

text.p: Crude tanker rates held steady on Wednesday, with Mediterranean 80,000 tonne vessels consolidating their strong gains over the past 10 days, brokers said.
In the Med, rates for 130,000 tonne ships started to rise to about W95/97.5 from about W90 as tonnage was lured away onto West African trips, they added.
"Some people are fixing from West Africa, so tonnage is disappearing from the Med," an Italian broker said.
Brokers said 80,000 tonne cross-Med vessels were fixed at about W150, down about 20 points from the highs achieved a few days ago, but well up from the W100 level seen in mid-January.

Middle East rates were generally steady, with very large crude carriers (VLCCs) on westward voyages at W55 and to Japan at W65. But to Singapore they were down slightly at W52.5 on good availability of tonnage, brokers said.
VLCCs from West Africa to the U.S. Gulf and from the North Sea to the U.S. were likewise little changed at about W62.5. On these routes 130,000 tonne vessels continued to be fixed at W95.

The inter-U.K./Cont market was stable, with 80,000 tonners fixed at W115, while 20,000 tonne fuel oil vessels remained at W195. But in the Med 20,000 tonnes of fuel oil was fixed down at W180 from W190.
In the western hemisphere Caribs/upcoast 70,000 tonners were little changed at W162.5/165.
